Oxford's ELR page (src-13) exempts native English speakers who have always been resident and citizens of a UKVI-recognised majority English-speaking country. gov.uk's Immigration Rules Appendix English Language, EL 4.1 (src-14, official_government, independently fetched) confirms the United States of America is on that list. US-track applicants who meet the residency/citizenship test are therefore exempt; those who do not (e.g. non-US-citizen attending a US school) need the standard test thresholds or another general exemption route. This resolves a genuine research gap with real evidence, not a guess.

verification_records.proposed_value: fixed_amount (reviewed and retained -- see notes)
verification_records.conflict_or_limitation_notes: Independently re-fetched src-08 this pass and reviewed the award_type classification per item 5's instruction. Confirmed verbatim: the Oxford Bursary is 'a non-repayable Oxford Bursary to help with the costs of studying and living in Oxford,' paid as one of five fixed GBP amounts selected by a household-income band (a step function: GBP4,480/3,930/3,360/2,230/1,120), not a continuously variable amount. Considered 'living_cost_support' as an alternative given the living-cost framing, but the source explicitly frames the award as covering BOTH study and living costs (broader than living_cost_support alone), and -- more importantly -- every recipient still receives ONE specific, discrete GBP figure rather than a percentage of fees, an open-ended reimbursement, or a periodic stipend. 'fixed_amount' remains the best-fit enum value; the income-banding is a matter of which fixed amount a given recipient qualifies for, not a departure from the fixed_amount structure. Value retained unchanged in records-v1.2.json; this VR documents the review as instructed.

Re-confirmed verbatim: '£1,529 per month (for up to 9 months) for courses in London' / '£1,171 per month (for up to 9 months) for courses outside London,' and that the applicable rate depends on where the COURSE is located, not where the student resides. This is suggestive (Oxford, ~90km from London and not one of the 32 boroughs, would fall under 'outside London' by elimination from this definition) but gov.uk still does NOT name Oxford anywhere on the page, so this pass treats it as a logical inference, not an official confirmation, and per the task's explicit instruction not to guess an immigration-relevant rate, records-v1.2.json's oxford_region_classification text is left unmodified at 'UNCONFIRMED' -- this VR both reconfirms the underlying monthly-range figures at VERIFIED and reconfirms that the UNCONFIRMED characterization remains accurate today, while noting the definitional-elimination reasoning above for whoever picks this up next. vr-12/vr-13 (the prior pass's canonical-field VRs for this same entity) were left untouched per instructions; this is a new, additive material_extension_fact record.
